summary: The game's pack (InventoryState kinds, whole units) against the survival core's items (items.json ids, their own units). SurvivalBridge eats through this table: one pack unit is `qty` of the core item. Food lives in the game's pack; the core's own inventory keeps the clothes and the rest of the kit (worn clothing sets warmth) until the two packs are merged.

jerky.note: a pound of jerked meat (280 game kcal, about a third of a meal)

cornmeal.note: a pound; must be cooked (a fire, next)

corn.note: an ear of flint corn from a bed (FarmField, 82 game kcal); must be cooked (roast it on a fire), or pound 4 into cornmeal

roast_corn.note: an ear roasted on a lit campfire (CampCooking): 82 game kcal

charred_corn.note: a roast that burnt: half the food

beans.note: a pound of dry beans from a bed (310 game kcal); must be cooked (boiled on a fire)

bean_pot.note: a pound of beans boiled (CampCooking): 2.6 lb of boiled beans, the same 310 game kcal

scorched_beans.note: a pot that caught: half the food

squash.note: a squash from a bed (80 game kcal, keeps for weeks); must be cooked (roasted on a fire)

roast_squash.note: a squash roasted in the ashes: 80 game kcal

charred_squash.note: a roast that burnt: half the food

venison.note: a meal's worth of fresh venison, 7 lb raw (770 game kcal); butchering gives a doe 4, a buck 5 (WildlifeSpecies). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach (items.json raw_risk)

blackberries.note: a handful (12 game kcal): berries are variety, not a living

crabapples.note: a handful of small sour apples (10 game kcal)

acorns.note: a handful, too bitter to eat until leached (forage.leach_acorns)

johnnycake.note: a pound of cornmeal baked in the ashes (cook.roast on a lit campfire; CampCooking): 1.5 lb of johnnycake, 330 game kcal

burnt_johnnycake.note: a roast that burnt: half the food (the core's rule: burnt food keeps half its energy)

roast_venison.note: a pack unit of venison roasted: 7 lb raw cook down to 5.9 lb (770 game kcal), no raw risk

charred_venison.note: a roast that burnt: half the food

small_game.note: 2 lb of fresh small game (240 game kcal): a hare dressed from a snare or a deadfall (TrapStation); a raccoon gives two, a furbearer one. Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

roast_small_game.note: a pack unit of small game roasted: 2 lb raw cook down to 1.7 lb (240 game kcal), no raw risk

charred_small_game.note: a roast that burnt: half the food

brook_trout.note: a pound of fresh brook trout (90 game kcal): a landed fish gives its weight in pounds, at least one (FishCatch). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

salmon.note: a pound of fresh Atlantic salmon (90 game kcal): a landed fish gives its weight in pounds, at least one (FishCatch). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

sucker.note: a pound of fresh white sucker (90 game kcal): a landed fish gives its weight in pounds, at least one (FishCatch). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

perch.note: a pound of fresh yellow perch (90 game kcal): a landed fish gives its weight in pounds, at least one (FishCatch). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

pike.note: a pound of fresh northern pike (90 game kcal): a landed fish gives its weight in pounds, at least one (FishCatch). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

eel.note: a pound of fresh American eel (90 game kcal): a landed fish gives its weight in pounds, at least one (FishCatch). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

bullhead.note: a pound of fresh brown bullhead (90 game kcal): a landed fish gives its weight in pounds, at least one (FishCatch). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

sturgeon.note: a pound of fresh lake sturgeon (90 game kcal): a landed fish gives its weight in pounds, at least one (FishCatch). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

pickerel.note: a pound of fresh chain pickerel (90 game kcal): a landed fish gives its weight in pounds, at least one (FishCatch). Raw: 1 in 10 turns the stomach

roast_fish.note: a pound of fresh fish roasted: 0.9 lb, the same 90 game kcal, no raw risk

charred_fish.note: a roast that burnt: half the food

cooking: CampCooking puts the pack's raw fish, venison, small game or cornmeal on a lit campfire (the core's cook.roast); each unit comes back as one unit of the cooked kind above (roast fish, roast venison, johnnycake), or the burnt one when the roast burns.

deer_hide.note: a deer's green hide from the knife (FieldDressing): the tanning frame scrapes it into rawhide or dresses it into buckskin (CampStation)

brains.note: a deer's brains (butchering): worked into a hide to dress it (rcp.dress_hide; cornmeal serves too)

cordage.note: a length of cord twisted from sinew (the workbench): one snare, or a rod's line

stake_set.note: deadfall stakes, trigger and bait stick (the workbench, rcp.stake_set): one deadfall

steel_trap.note: a steel trap (the kit's two; the trader later)

bar_lead.note: a pound of bar lead (casting balls at the fire was retired with the musket club and shot making, 2026-10-06)

bullet_mould.note: the bullet mould and ladle (the kit's)

hooks_line.note: hooks and line (the kit's): the rod's line and hook (the workbench)

sinew.note: a bundle of back sinew (butchering a deer gives 2): the thread of moccasins and mitts (the workbench)

wolf_pelt.note: a green wolf pelt from the knife: the stretching hoop dries it; the workbench sews mitts of it

dried_wolf_pelt.note: a wolf pelt stretched and dried on the hoop (fur.stretch, fur.dry)

bone_awl.note: an antler tine ground to a point (the knapping stone): the rules' awl for sewing while it is carried

flint_knife.note: a knapped flint knife (the knapping stone): the pack's, and the survival rules' knife while it is carried (SurvivalBridge.sync_carried_tools)

stone_axe.note: a stone axe (the knapping stone): the felling axe's work, slowly; the rules' axe for the deadfall while it is carried

dried_fox_pelt.note: a fox pelt stretched and dried on the hoop

bison_robe.note: a buffalo's green robe from the knife, the hair on: the tanning frame dresses it into a fur robe (rcp.dress_robe) that is worn and slept under

marten_pelt.note: a green marten pelt from the trap line (fur.skin): rich brown fur, the trade's best small fur: the stretching hoop dries it

mink_pelt.note: a green mink pelt from the trap line (fur.skin): the stretching hoop dries it

fisher_pelt.note: a green fisher pelt from the trap line (fur.skin): dark, heavy fur: the stretching hoop dries it

raccoon_pelt.note: a green raccoon pelt from the trap line (fur.skin): the stretching hoop dries it

dried_marten_pelt.note: a marten pelt stretched and dried on the hoop

dried_mink_pelt.note: a mink pelt stretched and dried on the hoop

dried_fisher_pelt.note: a fisher pelt stretched and dried on the hoop

dried_raccoon_pelt.note: a raccoon pelt stretched and dried on the hoop

climbing_stakes_wood.note: a pair of climbing stakes; the loadout carries them on the belt or sash (loadout_items.json)

climbing_claws_wood.note: a pair of grip claws; worn under the feet while climbing (loadout_items.json)

climbing_stakes_bone.note: a pair of climbing stakes; the loadout carries them on the belt or sash (loadout_items.json)

climbing_claws_bone.note: a pair of grip claws; worn under the feet while climbing (loadout_items.json)

climbing_stakes_stone.note: a pair of climbing stakes; the loadout carries them on the belt or sash (loadout_items.json)

climbing_claws_stone.note: a pair of grip claws; worn under the feet while climbing (loadout_items.json)

canoe_stake.note: a stake cut from a pole: the building bed of a canoe (the boat stand)

birch_bark_sheet.note: a whole sheet of birch bark, peeled in one piece: the skin of a bark canoe

wattap.note: a bundle of split conifer root: bark canoes are sewn with it

canoe_strip.note: a long strip split from a pole: a canoe's gunwales

canoe_rib.note: a thin rib split from a pole: set in a canoe under the gunwales

pine_pitch.note: pine resin: sealed into a canoe's seams with tallow and charcoal

firewood.note: a pack firewood on a campfire: an armload of split wood, 120 game minutes of fire (Campfire.FUEL_MIN_PER_WOOD; the fire's fuel is the core's record, CampLink)

start_gear_note: At a new game the background's trapping, shot-making and fishing gear (materials above) moves from the core's kit into the pack too, where it can be seen and used: the backcountry hunter's two steel traps, three pounds of bar lead, the mould, hooks and line, two sinew. The powder stays with the core's kit (by the pound: the fire's casting takes it).
start_food: At a new game the background's food (items above) moves from the core's inventory into the pack: the backcountry hunter's 6 lb of jerky and 8 lb of cornmeal.
eat_note: A pack unit is eaten whole (the stomach takes what fits); a unit over half again what the stomach has room for is refused as too much to eat now.
